summary.en: A former Hurras al-Din commander was arrested in Idlib, and Syrian officials warned that Druze groups, allegedly backed by Israel, may launch an offensive in Sweida. The YPJ said it remains a guarantee for security as Syria proceeds with its integration process, while defense universities limited women’s admission to most programs, a policy condemned by HRW. Jordan’s king reaffirmed support for Syria’s sovereignty and the Syrian Kurdish community expressed a preference for Bashar al-Assad over Erdogan. The UCDP recorded 2,732 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: En tidligere Hurras al-Din-kommandør ble arrestert i Idlib, og syriske myndigheter advarte om at drusgrupper, angivelig støttet av Israel, kan igangsette et offensiv i Sweida. YPJ sa at den fortsatt er en garanti for sikkerhet mens Syria fortsetter sin integrasjonsprosess, mens forsvarsuniversitetene begrenset kvinners opptak til de fleste programmer, en politikk som ble fordømt av HRW. Jordans konge bekreftet støtten til Syriens suverenitet og det syrisk-kurdiske samfunnet uttrykte en preferanse for Bashar al-Assad fremfor Erdogan. UCDP registrerte 2 732 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
background.extract: Disputes and clashes in Syria have continued following the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024, which many sources consider the end of the Syrian civil war. Numerous actors are involved, including clashes between the newly-formed Syrian caretaker government and later the Syrian transitional government led by the former emir of Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) and incumbent president Ahmed al-Sharaa, Assad loyalists, Alawite groups, and Druze insurgents; clashes between elements of the Turkish-backed Syrian National Army (SNA) and the government on one side, and formerly the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) on the other; as well as an Israeli invasion and occupation of the demilitarized buffer zone in southwestern Syria.
